title: Felix and the Wolf
premise: Marguerite Okafor, a scribe indentured to the Thornfell temple, has spent years copying prophecies while keeping their own past buried. When a smuggler named Felix arrives carrying a ledger that matches, word for word, a century-old prophecy about 'the scribe who remembers both names,' Marguerite realizes the covenant binding the human and wolf realms is failing—and that they were born to mend it. Pursued by temple inquisitors and the dying Wolf King's hunters alike, Marguerite and Felix cross the mountains to reforge the covenant at the Hollow Altar. In the end, Marguerite must sacrifice their erased memories—the last gift of their hidden heritage—to seal the pact, choosing love and duty together over the self they might have been.
about_author: B. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy rooted in borders, debts, and the people who live in between.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A night of routine smuggling through Thornfell's passes introduces Felix, whose payment ledger bears script identical to a prophecy Marguerite copied that morning. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the first crack in a carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the temple archive, Marguerite finds their own handwriting in a book written a hundred years before their birth. An inquisitor notices the discrepancy. The beat is vertigo—identity itself becomes unreliable.

chapters.title: What the Wolf King Owes
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix reveals he serves the fading Wolf King, whose realm is unraveling as the covenant decays; his ledger records debts owed across realms, including one against Marguerite's bloodline. The beat is reluctant alliance forged from mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: Debt-Bound
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The temple brands Marguerite a heretic and calls in their indenture; flight becomes the only option. Felix breaks them out through smuggler roads only Marguerite knows. The beat is grief for the life abandoned, sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Pass Where Names Change
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Crossing a border pass where memories blur, each glimpses the other's buried past—Felix's broken oath, Marguerite's stolen childhood name. The beat is intimacy born of exposure neither can undo.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Hollow Altar
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Temple inquisitors and the Wolf King's renegade hunters converge on the pair; an ambush costs them their supplies and nearly their trust. The beat is fear curdling into the realization that someone inside the Wolf King's court wants the covenant dead.

chapters.title: A Century of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Sheltering with a hermit archivist, Marguerite learns the full prophecy: the covenant was broken deliberately by the temple's founders, and Marguerite's lineage was engineered to repair it—or be destroyed trying. The beat is fury transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Toll
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The traitor revealed is Felix's own handler, who offers Felix absolution if he delivers Marguerite instead. Felix refuses, burning his debt-ledger. The beat is love openly declared against duty's oldest claim.

chapters.title: Reforge the Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the Hollow Altar, realms fraying around them, Marguerite performs the reforging rite—but it demands memory as fuel. As inquisitors breach the altar, Marguerite feeds it their erased heritage, name by name. The beat is sacrificial climax, terror and transcendence entwined.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Road
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The covenant holds; the realms knit closed. Marguerite remembers little of what they lost but chooses to begin again, walking out of Thornfell beside Felix with a blank page where the prophecy once stood. The beat is bittersweet peace: identity rebuilt not from the past, but from love.
